per_question.question: Did bla OXA-244 predominate and reside mainly on the chromosome in the pediatric cancer patient E. coli isolates?
per_question.answer: Yes. In the collection of 20 bloodstream E. coli isolates from pediatric cancer patients, the OXA‑244 variant was the most common OXA‑48‑like gene and was found mainly integrated in the chromosome rather than on plasmids[PMID:42005841].

per_question.question: Is the mcr-9 gene detected in multidrug‑resistant uropathogenic Escherichia coli isolates from urinary tract infection patients?
per_question.answer:
Screening of 88 multidrug‑resistant uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) isolates from urine samples showed that none carried the mcr‑9 gene; all isolates were colistin‑susceptible and mcr‑9 was absent[PMID:40708009].  

A separate investigation of ESBL‑producing Enterobacteriaceae from clinical specimens did identify a silent mcr‑9 in a single E. coli urine isolate, but this study did not focus on a defined MDR‑UPEC cohort[PMID:41252401].  Hence, in the specific set of MDR‑UPEC isolates examined, mcr‑9 was not detected.

per_question.question: What is the prevalence of co-occurrence of blaTEM and blaCTX-M among ESBL-producing uropathogenic E. coli isolates from ICU patients in Tabriz, Iran?
per_question.answer: Among the 48 ESBL‑producing uropathogenic E. coli isolates recovered from ICU patients in Tabriz, 18 isolates harboured both bla_TEM and bla_CTX‑M, corresponding to a co‑occurrence prevalence of **37.5 %** of ESBL producers[PMID:42819557].

per_question.question: What are the reported conjugation transfer efficiencies of the bla NDM-1–harboring IncFII plasmid from Salmonella Derby and Escherichia coli isolates?
per_question.answer: The IncFII plasmid carrying bla NDM‑1 transferred from the carbapenem‑resistant **Salmonella Derby** isolate to a recipient at an efficiency of **(4.50 ± 1.29) × 10⁻²**. The same plasmid transferred from the co‑isolated **Escherichia coli** strain at a higher efficiency of **(3.17 ± 0.74) × 10⁻¹**[PMID:41878261].

per_question.question: How does incubation at 42°C affect the copy number of blaNDM-5 in bacterial membrane vesicles from pig-derived carbapenem-resistant E. coli?
per_question.answer: Incubation of the pig‑derived carbapenem‑resistant E. coli at 42 °C markedly enriches bla_NDM‑5 within the released membrane vesicles, raising the vesicular gene copy number by more than two‑fold compared with vesicles produced at 37 °C[PMID:42176434].

per_question.question: What is the role of blaTEM-1 and blaTEM-176 overexpression in ampicillin/sulbactam resistance of non-ESBL Salmonella from raw chicken?
per_question.answer: Overexpression of the bla_TEM‑1 and bla_TEM‑176 genes drives hyper‑production of TEM β‑lactamase in non‑ESBL Salmonella isolates from raw chicken, raising the ampicillin MIC by ≈5‑fold and thereby conferring resistance to the ampicillin/sulbactam (SAM) combination.  Host‑dependent up‑regulation of these genes was shown to be the key mechanism underlying the atypical SAM‑resistant phenotype, with an ampicillin MIC ≥1024 ppm predicting SAM resistance[PMID:41604208].

per_question.question: What percentage of freshwater fish were contaminated with colistin-resistant E. coli carrying the mcr-1 gene?
per_question.answer: About 24 % of the freshwater fish sampled were contaminated with colistin‑resistant E. coli that all harboured the plasmid‑mediated mcr‑1 gene (24.3 % of the 103 fish examined)[PMID:36166861].

per_question.question: Which plasmid type in the Indian Salmonella Typhi outbreak carries the bla NDM-5 gene?
per_question.answer: The outbreak isolates harbored the bla NDM‑5 gene on an IncX3 plasmid[PMID:41415828].

per_question.question: What proportion of mcr-1-positive avian pathogenic E. coli isolates from Algerian poultry belong to phylogroup B1?
per_question.answer: In the Algerian study, 41 mcr‑1‑positive avian pathogenic E. coli isolates were phylogrouped, and 76 % of them were assigned to phylogroup B1[PMID:42704645].

per_question.question: On which plasmid incompatibility group is the blaKPC-2 gene located in the Enterobacter kobei SCLZS19 isolate?
per_question.answer: The blaKPC‑2 gene in the Enterobacter kobei SCLZS19 isolate is located on a self‑transmissible IncP6 plasmid[PMID:37369327].

per_question.question: What is the sensitivity of the LAMP assay for detecting the fosA gene in Escherichia coli?
per_question.answer: The LAMP assay developed for the fosA resistance gene showed a sensitivity of **43 % when applied to *Escherichia coli* isolates**[PMID:42218183].

per_question.question: What is the limit of detection for blaCTX-M using nested PCR after 8 hours enrichment?
per_question.answer: The nested PCR (nPCR) assay achieved a limit of detection of **1 CFU per mL** for the bla<sub>CTX‑M</sub> gene after **8 hours of enrichment** in the selective medium[PMID:39335221].

per_question.question: What percentage of Escherichia coli isolates from Kawempe slum wastewater were resistant to at least one antibiotic?
per_question.answer: In the study of wastewater from Kawempe slums, 72.8 % of the Escherichia coli isolates (169 of 232) were resistant to at least one of the tested antibiotics[PMID:40399779].

per_question.question: Which dfr gene variants were detected in the trimethoprim‑sulfamethoxazole‑resistant E. coli isolates?
per_question.answer: The study of urinary‑tract isolates found that among the trimethoprim‑sulfamethoxazole‑resistant E. coli, the dihydrofolate‑reductase genes dfrA5 were present in several isolates and dfrA1 was detected in one isolate; the other screened variant (dfrA7/17) was not reported among the resistant strains [PMID:42626150].
unsupported_claims: The other screened variant dfrA7/17 was not reported among the resistant strains.

per_question.question: What were the resistance rates to enrofloxacin and ciprofloxacin among AcrAB‑TolC‑positive avian pathogenic E. coli isolates from diseased poultry?
per_question.answer: Among the 30 AcrAB‑TolC‑positive avian pathogenic E. coli isolates recovered from diseased poultry, resistance to both enrofloxacin and ciprofloxacin was observed in all strains, giving a resistance rate of 100 % for each fluoroquinolone[PMID:41489466].

per_question.question: Which quorum-sensing system is described as the primary AI-2 pathway in uropathogenic Escherichia coli?
per_question.answer: The primary AI‑2 quorum‑sensing pathway in uropathogenic Escherichia coli is the LuxS‑dependent autoinducer‑2 (AI‑2) system[PMID:41750267].
unsupported_claims: The primary AI‑2 quorum‑sensing pathway in uropathogenic Escherichia coli is the LuxS‑dependent autoinducer‑2 (AI‑2) system.

per_question.question: What procalcitonin level is identified as a predictor of septic shock in acute obstructive pyelonephritis?
per_question.answer: Elevated procalcitonin greater than 1.12 µg/L has been reported as a predictor of septic shock in patients with acute obstructive pyelonephritis[PMID:41597508].

per_question.question: What share of infections at An-Najah National University Hospital in Palestine were caused by ESBL-producing E. coli?
per_question.answer: At An‑Najah National University Hospital, ESBL‑producing *Escherichia coli* were responsible for the majority of infections, accounting for **62.8 %** of the cases reported in the 2021 cohort[PMID:38321071].

per_question.question: What percentage of Enterobacter cloacae isolates from Polish retail animal-origin foods were resistant to ampicillin?
per_question.answer: In Polish retail foods of animal origin, 76.9 % of the Enterobacter cloacae isolates were resistant to ampicillin[PMID:41064398].

per_question.question: Which metabolic pathway does 18AA activate to enhance ceftazidime‑avibactam activity against carbapenem‑resistant Escherichia coli?
per_question.answer: 18AA potentiates ceftazidime‑avibactam by reprogramming bacterial metabolism and strongly activating the pyruvate cycle, which raises NADH production and the proton‑motive force, thereby increasing intracellular drug accumulation in carbapenem‑resistant E. coli[PMID:42852341].

per_question.question: What proportion of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales isolates were resistant to mecillinam in the 2023 Marrakech study?
per_question.answer: In the 2023 Marrakech study, 64 % of the 180 carbapenemase‑producing Enterobacterales isolates were resistant to mecillinam[PMID:42306523].

per_question.question: What proportion of STEC and EHEC isolates from Brazilian beef cattle carried the stx2 gene?
per_question.answer: Among the STEC and EHEC isolates obtained from Brazilian beef cattle (n = 24), the stx2 gene was detected in 21 isolates, corresponding to 21/24 ≈ 87.5 % of the isolates[PMID:42231163].

per_question.question: Which antibiotic classes exhibited notable resistance among isolates from the integrated chicken and fish farming system in Bangladesh?
per_question.answer: The isolates from the integrated chicken‑fish farming system showed especially high resistance to **tetracycline‑type antibiotics** and **fluoroquinolones**[PMID:41950191].

per_question.question: In Gram-negative bloodstream infections at a tertiary hospital in eastern India, which factor independently predicted difficult-to-treat resistance?
per_question.answer: Prior antibiotic use was the only factor that remained independently associated with difficult‑to‑treat resistance in Gram‑negative bloodstream infections at the tertiary hospital in eastern India[PMID:42544149].

per_question.question: What independent risk factors are associated with multidrug‑resistant infections among adults with chronic hepatic disease?
per_question.answer: In adults with chronic hepatic disease, multivariate analysis identified several independent predictors of multidrug‑resistant (MDR) infection: age > 60 years, male gender, acquisition of the infection in a healthcare setting, a Gram‑negative bacterial etiology, and prior exposure to antibiotics [PMID:42051708].

per_question.question: How did resistance to last-resort beta-lactams change over a decade among urinary pathogens in South Korean hospitals?
per_question.answer:
Over the ten‑year period (2012‑2021) carbapenems – the last‑resort β‑lactams for urinary isolates – showed divergent trends in the two dominant uropathogens.  In *Escherichia coli* the prevalence of ertapenem resistance stayed very low, rising only from 0.3 % to 1.2 % and never reaching a clinically significant level[PMID:40870856].  By contrast, *Klebsiella pneumoniae* displayed a marked increase: ertapenem resistance climbed from 3.0 % to 18.1 % and imipenem resistance from 0.4 % to 16.8 % over the same decade, driven largely by ESBL‑producing strains[PMID:40870856].

A later single‑center series (2016‑2024) confirmed the upward trajectory, reporting a steady rise in carbapenem resistance among both *E. coli* and *K. pneumoniae* (annual percentage change ≈ 22 %) despite the overall rates remaining lower than for other agents[PMID:42405714].  Thus, while carbapenem (last‑resort β‑lactam) resistance remained minimal in *E. coli*, it escalated substantially in *K. pneumoniae* across a decade of Korean hospital urinary isolates.

per_question.question: Can Trichomonas vaginalis somatic proteins kill Staphylococcus species while sparing Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica?
per_question.answer: Yes. Somatic proteins from *Trichomonas vaginalis* (TvSP) rapidly kill Gram‑positive *Staphylococcus* species (including *S. aureus*, *S. warneri* and *S. saprophyticus*) by damaging their cell walls, yet they show no antibacterial activity against the Gram‑negative *Escherichia coli* or *Salmonella enterica* under the same in‑vitro conditions[PMID:42229695].

per_question.question: What bacterial pathogens are being considered for future maternal vaccines to lower neonatal sepsis rates?
per_question.answer: Future maternal vaccines under development aim to target the bacterial pathogens most responsible for neonatal sepsis, specifically Group B Streptococcus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli [PMID:41176483]. By inducing maternal antibodies that are transferred to the infant, these candidate vaccines could reduce the incidence of early‑onset sepsis caused by these organisms and consequently lower the need for broad‑spectrum antibiotics in newborns.

per_question.question: How common is polymyxin E resistance among poultry-disease isolates from farms in Sargodha, Jhang and Toba Tek Singh?
per_question.answer: Colistin (polymyxin E) resistance was detected in roughly one‑quarter of the avian pathogenic isolates collected from the three Punjab districts, with an overall prevalence of 24.78 % (95 % CI 19.6‑30.7 %) among the 230 visceral organ samples examined[PMID:40777829]. The frequency differed markedly by location: 42 % of isolates from Jhang were colistin‑resistant, 23.61 % from Sargodha, and only 5.55 % from Toba Tek Singh[PMID:40777829].

per_question.question: In the Romanian cohort, which sex had a higher prevalence of resistant urinary isolates in complicated kidney infections?
per_question.answer: In the Romanian cohort of patients with complicated acute pyelonephritis, resistant urinary isolates were observed more often in men than in women[PMID:42075164].

per_question.question: On Belgian farms, in which animals were cephalosporin-resistant gut bacteria found most often?
per_question.answer: Cephalosporin‑resistant gut bacteria were detected most frequently in broiler chickens; ESBL‑producing E. coli were found in 10 % of broiler ceca (and 2.5 % of the broiler environment), a markedly higher prevalence than in pigs (≈1 % feces), cattle (≈1 % feces) or calves (≈1 % feces) on the same Belgian farms[PMID:42149085].

per_question.question: What is the prevalence of nasal versus rectovaginal colonization with methicillin‑resistant Staphylococcus aureus among delivering mothers in eastern Sri Lanka?
per_question.answer: In the cross‑sectional study of 235 delivering mothers at the Teaching Hospital, Batticaloa (Eastern Province, Sri Lanka), MRSA was found in 33 women (14 %). Site‑specific prevalence was 12 women (5.1 %) with nasal colonisation and 24 women (10.2 %) with rectovaginal colonisation[PMID:41692738].

per_question.question: Can oral amoxicillin-clavulanate monotherapy after initial IV treatment prevent renal scarring in infants with ESBL-producing E. coli urinary tract infection?
per_question.answer: Yes. In a report of two infants (3 months and 8 months old) with ESBL‑producing E. coli urinary tract infection, fever resolved after an initial course of intravenous cefotaxime and the patients were then switched to oral amoxicillin‑clavulanate (14:1) monotherapy for a total of two weeks. Chronic‑phase technetium‑99m dimercaptosuccinic acid renal scintigraphy performed after treatment showed no renal scarring in either child[PMID:39725072].
